L16: ## 27.13 Projective space
L17: 
L18: Projective space is one of the fundamental objects studied in algebraic geometry. In this section we just give its construction as $\text{Proj}$ of a polynomial ring. Later we will discover many of its beautiful properties.
L19: 
L20: 【11†Lemma 27.13.1.】 Let $S = \mathbf{Z}[T_0, \ldots , T_ n]$ with $\deg (T_ i) = 1$. The scheme
L21: 
L22: \[ \mathbf{P}^ n_{\mathbf{Z}} = \text{Proj}(S) \]
L23: 
L24: represents the functor which associates to a scheme $Y$ the pairs $(\mathcal{L}, (s_0, \ldots , s_ n))$ where
L25:   1. $\mathcal{L}$ is an invertible $\mathcal{O}_ Y$-module, and
L26: 
L27:   2. $s_0, \ldots , s_ n$ are global sections of $\mathcal{L}$ which generate $\mathcal{L}$
L28: 
L29: up to the following equivalence: $(\mathcal{L}, (s_0, \ldots , s_ n)) \sim (\mathcal{N}, (t_0, \ldots , t_ n))$ $\Leftrightarrow $ there exists an isomorphism $\beta : \mathcal{L} \to \mathcal{N}$ with $\beta (s_ i) = t_ i$ for $i = 0, \ldots , n$.
L30: 
L31: Proof. This is a special case of Lemma 【12†27.12.3】 above. Namely, for any graded ring $A$ we have
L32: \begin{eqnarray*} \mathop{\mathrm{Mor}}\nolimits _{graded rings}(\mathbf{Z}[T_0, \ldots , T_ n], A) & = & A_1 \times \ldots \times A_1 \\ \psi & \mapsto & (\psi (T_0), \ldots , \psi (T_ n)) \end{eqnarray*}
L33: 
L34: and the degree $1$ part of $\Gamma _*(Y, \mathcal{L})$ is just $\Gamma (Y, \mathcal{L})$. $\square$
L35: 【13†Definition 27.13.2.】 The scheme $\mathbf{P}^ n_{\mathbf{Z}} = \text{Proj}(\mathbf{Z}[T_0, \ldots , T_ n])$ is called projective $n$-space over $\mathbf{Z}$. Its base change $\mathbf{P}^ n_ S$ to a scheme $S$ is called projective $n$-space over $S$. If $R$ is a ring the base change to $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(R)$ is denoted $\mathbf{P}^ n_ R$ and called projective $n$-space over $R$.
L36: Given a scheme $Y$ over $S$ and a pair $(\mathcal{L}, (s_0, \ldots , s_ n))$ as in Lemma 【11†27.13.1】 the induced morphism to $\mathbf{P}^ n_ S$ is denoted
L37: 
L38: \[ \varphi _{(\mathcal{L}, (s_0, \ldots , s_ n))} : Y \longrightarrow \mathbf{P}^ n_ S \]
L39: This makes sense since the pair defines a morphism into $\mathbf{P}^ n_{\mathbf{Z}}$ and we already have the structure morphism into $S$ so combined we get a morphism into $\mathbf{P}^ n_ S = \mathbf{P}^ n_{\mathbf{Z}} \times S$. Via Lemma 【14†27.16.10】 we can identify $\mathbf{P}^ n_ S$ with a relative Proj of the graded $\mathcal{O}_ S$-algebra $\mathcal{O}_ S[T_0, \ldots , T_ n]$ and we can characterize $\varphi _{(\mathcal{L}, (s_0, \ldots , s_ n))}$ as the unique $S$-morphism such that

L44: 【16†Lemma 27.13.3.】 Projective $n$-space over $\mathbf{Z}$ is covered by $n + 1$ standard opens
L45: \[ \mathbf{P}^ n_{\mathbf{Z}} = \bigcup \nolimits _{i = 0, \ldots , n} D_{+}(T_ i) \]

L49: Proof. This is true because $\mathbf{Z}[T_0, \ldots , T_ n]_{+} = (T_0, \ldots , T_ n)$ and since

L51: \[ \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}\left( \mathbf{Z} \left[\frac{T_0}{T_ i}, \ldots , \frac{T_ n}{T_ i} \right] \right) \cong \mathbf{A}^ n_{\mathbf{Z}} \]

L54: 【17†Lemma 27.13.4.】 Let $S$ be a scheme. The structure morphism $\mathbf{P}^ n_ S \to S$ is
L55: 
L56:   1. separated,
L57: 
L58:   2. quasi-compact,
L59: 
L60:   3. satisfies the existence and uniqueness parts of the valuative criterion, and
L61: 
L62:   4. universally closed.
L63: Proof. All these properties are stable under base change (this is clear for the last two and for the other two see Schemes, Lemmas 【18†26.21.12】 and 【19†26.19.3】). Hence it suffices to prove them for the morphism $\mathbf{P}^ n_{\mathbf{Z}} \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(\mathbf{Z})$. Separatedness is Lemma 【20†27.8.8】. Quasi-compactness follows from Lemma 【16†27.13.3】. Existence and uniqueness of the valuative criterion follow from Lemma 【21†27.8.11】.
L64: Universally closed follows from the above and Schemes, Proposition 【22†26.20.6】. $\square$

L67: 【24†Lemma 27.13.6 (Segre embedding).】 Let $S$ be a scheme. There exists a closed immersion
L68: \[ \mathbf{P}^ n_ S \times _ S \mathbf{P}^ m_ S \longrightarrow \mathbf{P}^{nm + n + m}_ S \]
L69: 
L70: called the Segre embedding.
L71: Proof. It suffices to prove this when $S = \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(\mathbf{Z})$. Hence we will drop the index $S$ and work in the absolute setting. Write $\mathbf{P}^ n = \text{Proj}(\mathbf{Z}[X_0, \ldots , X_ n])$, $\mathbf{P}^ m = \text{Proj}(\mathbf{Z}[Y_0, \ldots , Y_ m])$, and $\mathbf{P}^{nm + n + m} = \text{Proj}(\mathbf{Z}[Z_0, \ldots , Z_{nm + n + m}])$.
